import Mathlib.Logic.Equiv.Defs
import ConNF.Base.NearLitter

/-!
# Base permutations

In this file, we define the group of *base permutations*, and their actions on atoms, litters, and
near-litters. In the paper, these are called *`-1`-allowable permutations*, but that term has a
different meaning in this formalisation.
-/

universe u

open Cardinal Equiv
open scoped Pointwise

namespace ConNF

variable [Params.{u}]

/-!
## Definitions
-/

/-- A *base permutation* consists of a permutation of atoms, a permutation of litters, and a proof
that if some set `s` is near the litter set of some litter `L`, then when we apply the permutation
of atoms pointwise to `s`, the resulting set of atoms is near the litter obtained by applying the
permutation of litters to `L`. This condition means that the pointwise image of a near-litter `N`
under the permutation of atoms is a near-litter, and that the litter it is near to is just the image
of `Nᴸ` under the permutation of litters. It is easy to see that it is not necessary to include
the litter permutation in this definition, because the image of some litter `L` under the
permutation of litters must be the unique litter near the pointwise image of `Lᴬ` under the map of
atoms; we simply include the data of this extra permutation for definitional convenience. -/
structure BasePerm where
  atoms : Perm Atom
  litters : Perm Litter
  apply_near_apply (s : Set Atom) (L : Litter) : s ~ Lᴬ → atoms '' s ~ (litters L)ᴬ

namespace BasePerm

/-- If `π` is a base permutation, we write `πᴬ` for its associated permutation of atoms. -/
instance : SuperA BasePerm (Perm Atom) where
  superA := atoms

/-- If `π` is a base permutation, we write `πᴸ` for its associated permutation of litters. -/
instance : SuperL BasePerm (Perm Litter) where
  superL := litters

/-- For a base permutation `π` and an atom `a`, we write `π • a` for `πᴬ a`.
We will later show that this is a group action. -/
instance : SMul BasePerm Atom where
  smul π a := πᴬ a

/-- For a base permutation `π` and a litter `L`, we write `π • L` for `πᴸ L`.
We will later show that this is a group action. -/
instance : SMul BasePerm Litter where
  smul π L := πᴸ L

/-- A restatement of `apply_near_apply` using the new notations. -/
theorem smul_near_smul (π : BasePerm) (s : Set Atom) (L : Litter) :
    s ~ Lᴬ → π • s ~ (π • L)ᴬ :=
  π.apply_near_apply s L

/-- For a base permutation `π` and an atom `N`, we write `π • N` for the near-litter `N'` such that
`N'ᴸ = π • Nᴸ` and `N'ᴬ = π • Nᴬ`, where the latter group action on sets of atoms is the pointwise
action. We will later show that this is a group action. -/
instance : SMul BasePerm NearLitter where
  smul π N := ⟨π • Nᴸ, π • Nᴬ, π.smul_near_smul Nᴬ Nᴸ N.atoms_near_litter⟩

/-! We establish some useful definitional equalities. -/

theorem smul_atom_def (π : BasePerm) (a : Atom) :
    π • a = πᴬ a :=
  rfl

theorem smul_litter_def (π : BasePerm) (L : Litter) :
    π • L = πᴸ L :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem smul_nearLitter_atoms (π : BasePerm) (N : NearLitter) :
    (π • N)ᴬ = π • Nᴬ :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem smul_nearLitter_litter (π : BasePerm) (N : NearLitter) :
    (π • N)ᴸ = π • Nᴸ :=
  rfl

/-- An extensionality principle for base permutations: if two base permutations have the same
action on atoms, then they coincide. This is because we can recover the data of `πᴸ` from `πᴬ`,
given that `π` is a base permutation. -/
@[ext]
theorem ext {π₁ π₂ : BasePerm} (h : ∀ a : Atom, π₁ • a = π₂ • a) :
    π₁ = π₂ := by
  obtain ⟨πa₁, πl₁, h₁⟩ := π₁
  obtain ⟨πa₂, πl₂, h₂⟩ := π₂
  rw [mk.injEq]
  have : πa₁ = πa₂ := by ext a; exact h a
  refine ⟨this, ?_⟩
  ext L
  have h₁' := h₁ Lᴬ L near_rfl
  have h₂' := h₂ Lᴬ L near_rfl
  rw [this] at h₁'
  exact litter_eq_of_near <| near_trans (near_symm h₁') h₂'

/-!
## Group structure
-/

/-- The identity permutation. -/
instance : One BasePerm where
  one := ⟨1, 1, λ s L h ↦ by simpa only [Perm.coe_one, id_eq, Set.image_id']⟩

@[simp]
theorem one_atom :
    (1 : BasePerm)ᴬ = 1 :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem one_litter :
    (1 : BasePerm)ᴸ = 1 :=
  rfl

/-- The composition of permutations. -/
instance : Mul BasePerm where
  mul π₁ π₂ := ⟨π₁ᴬ * π₂ᴬ, π₁ᴸ * π₂ᴸ, λ s L h ↦ by
    have := π₁.smul_near_smul _ _ <| π₂.smul_near_smul s L h
    simpa only [Set.smul_set_def, Set.image_image] using this⟩

@[simp]
theorem mul_atom (π₁ π₂ : BasePerm) :
    (π₁ * π₂)ᴬ = π₁ᴬ * π₂ᴬ :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem mul_litter (π₁ π₂ : BasePerm) :
    (π₁ * π₂)ᴸ = π₁ᴸ * π₂ᴸ :=
  rfl

/-- The relevant instance of `smul_near_smul` for the inverse of a base permutation. -/
theorem inv_smul_near_inv_smul (π : BasePerm) (s : Set Atom) (L : Litter) :
    s ~ Lᴬ → πᴬ⁻¹ • s ~ (πᴸ⁻¹ • L)ᴬ := by
  intro h
  apply near_trans (near_image h ↑πᴬ⁻¹)
  have := π.smul_near_smul (πᴸ⁻¹ L)ᴬ (πᴸ⁻¹ L) near_rfl
  have := near_image this ↑πᴬ⁻¹
  simp only [smul_litter_def, smul_atom_def, Perm.apply_inv_self, Set.smul_set_def,
    Perm.image_inv, preimage_image] at this
  rw [Perm.image_inv]
  exact near_symm this

/-- The inverse of a permutation. -/
instance : Inv BasePerm where
  inv π := ⟨πᴬ⁻¹, πᴸ⁻¹, π.inv_smul_near_inv_smul⟩

@[simp]
theorem inv_atom (π : BasePerm) :
    π⁻¹ᴬ = πᴬ⁻¹ :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem inv_litter (π : BasePerm) :
    π⁻¹ᴸ = πᴸ⁻¹ :=
  rfl

/-- The group structure on base permutations. -/
instance : Group BasePerm where
  mul_assoc π₁ π₂ π₃ := by
    ext a
    simp only [smul_atom_def, mul_atom, mul_assoc]
  one_mul π := by
    ext a
    simp only [smul_atom_def, mul_atom, one_atom, one_mul]
  mul_one π := by
    ext a
    simp only [smul_atom_def, mul_atom, one_atom, mul_one]
  inv_mul_cancel π := by
    ext a
    simp only [smul_atom_def, mul_atom, inv_atom, inv_mul_cancel, Perm.coe_one, id_eq, one_atom]

/-- The action of base permutations on atoms is a group action. -/
instance : MulAction BasePerm Atom where
  one_smul _ := rfl
  mul_smul _ _ _ := rfl

/-- The action of base permutations on litters is a group action. -/
instance : MulAction BasePerm Litter where
  one_smul _ := rfl
  mul_smul _ _ _ := rfl

/-- The action of base permutations on near-litters is a group action. -/
instance : MulAction BasePerm NearLitter where
  one_smul N := by
    ext a
    simp only [smul_nearLitter_atoms, one_smul]
  mul_smul π₁ π₂ N := by
    ext a
    simp only [smul_nearLitter_atoms, mul_smul]

/-- Base permutations commute with the interference of near-litters. -/
@[simp]
theorem smul_interference (π : BasePerm) (N₁ N₂ : NearLitter) :
    π • interference N₁ N₂ = interference (π • N₁) (π • N₂) := by
  exact?

action on atoms, then they coincide. This is because we can recover the data of `πᴸ` from `πᴬ`,
given that `π` is a base permutation. -/

theorem ext {π₁ π₂ : BasePerm} (h : ∀ a : Atom, π₁ • a = π₂ • a) :
    π₁ = π₂ := by

  refine ⟨this, ?_⟩
  ext L

  have h₂' := h₂ Lᴬ L near_rfl
  rw [this] at h₁'
  exact litter_eq_of_near <| near_trans (near_symm h₁') h₂'

import Mathlib.Logic.Equiv.Defs

/-!
# Base permutations

In this file, we define the group of *base permutations*, and their actions on atoms, litters, and
near-litters. In the paper, these are called *`-1`-allowable permutations*, but that term has a
different meaning in this formalisation.
-/

universe u

open Cardinal Equiv
open scoped Pointwise

namespace ConNF

variable [Params.{u}]

/-!
## Definitions
-/

/-- A *base permutation* consists of a permutation of atoms, a permutation of litters, and a proof
that if some set `s` is near the litter set of some litter `L`, then when we apply the permutation
of atoms pointwise to `s`, the resulting set of atoms is near the litter obtained by applying the
permutation of litters to `L`. This condition means that the pointwise image of a near-litter `N`
under the permutation of atoms is a near-litter, and that the litter it is near to is just the image
of `Nᴸ` under the permutation of litters. It is easy to see that it is not necessary to include
the litter permutation in this definition, because the image of some litter `L` under the
permutation of litters must be the unique litter near the pointwise image of `Lᴬ` under the map of
atoms; we simply include the data of this extra permutation for definitional convenience. -/
structure BasePerm where
  atoms : Perm Atom
  litters : Perm Litter
  apply_near_apply (s : Set Atom) (L : Litter) : s ~ Lᴬ → atoms '' s ~ (litters L)ᴬ

namespace BasePerm

/-- If `π` is a base permutation, we write `πᴬ` for its associated permutation of atoms. -/
instance : SuperA BasePerm (Perm Atom) where
  superA := atoms

/-- If `π` is a base permutation, we write `πᴸ` for its associated permutation of litters. -/
instance : SuperL BasePerm (Perm Litter) where
  superL := litters

/-- For a base permutation `π` and an atom `a`, we write `π • a` for `πᴬ a`.
We will later show that this is a group action. -/
instance : SMul BasePerm Atom where
  smul π a := πᴬ a

/-- For a base permutation `π` and a litter `L`, we write `π • L` for `πᴸ L`.
We will later show that this is a group action. -/
instance : SMul BasePerm Litter where
  smul π L := πᴸ L

/-- A restatement of `apply_near_apply` using the new notations. -/
theorem smul_near_smul (π : BasePerm) (s : Set Atom) (L : Litter) :
    s ~ Lᴬ → π • s ~ (π • L)ᴬ :=
  π.apply_near_apply s L

/-- For a base permutation `π` and an atom `N`, we write `π • N` for the near-litter `N'` such that
`N'ᴸ = π • Nᴸ` and `N'ᴬ = π • Nᴬ`, where the latter group action on sets of atoms is the pointwise
action. We will later show that this is a group action. -/
instance : SMul BasePerm NearLitter where
  smul π N := ⟨π • Nᴸ, π • Nᴬ, π.smul_near_smul Nᴬ Nᴸ N.atoms_near_litter⟩

    π • a = πᴬ a :=
  rfl

theorem smul_litter_def (π : BasePerm) (L : Litter) :
    π • L = πᴸ L :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem smul_nearLitter_atoms (π : BasePerm) (N : NearLitter) :
    (π • N)ᴬ = π • Nᴬ :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem smul_nearLitter_litter (π : BasePerm) (N : NearLitter) :
    (π • N)ᴸ = π • Nᴸ :=
  rfl

action on atoms, then they coincide. This is because we can recover the data of `πᴸ` from `πᴬ`,

/-- An extensionality principle for base permutations: if two base permutations have the same
action on atoms, then they coincide. This is because we can recover the data of `πᴸ` from `πᴬ`,
given that `π` is a base permutation. -/
@[ext]
theorem ext {π₁ π₂ : BasePerm} (h : ∀ a : Atom, π₁ • a = π₂ • a) :
    π₁ = π₂ := by
  obtain ⟨πa₁, πl₁, h₁⟩ := π₁
  obtain ⟨πa₂, πl₂, h₂⟩ := π₂

  refine ⟨this, ?_⟩
  ext L
  have h₁' := h₁ Lᴬ L near_rfl
  have h₂' := h₂ Lᴬ L near_rfl
  rw [this] at h₁'
  exact litter_eq_of_near <| near_trans (near_symm h₁') h₂'

import Mathlib.Logic.Equiv.Defs
import ConNF.Base.NearLitter

/-!
# Base permutations

In this file, we define the group of *base permutations*, and their actions on atoms, litters, and
near-litters. In the paper, these are called *`-1`-allowable permutations*, but that term has a
different meaning in this formalisation.
-/

universe u

open Cardinal Equiv
open scoped Pointwise

namespace ConNF

variable [Params.{u}]

/-!
## Definitions
-/

/-- A *base permutation* consists of a permutation of atoms, a permutation of litters, and a proof
that if some set `s` is near the litter set of some litter `L`, then when we apply the permutation
of atoms pointwise to `s`, the resulting set of atoms is near the litter obtained by applying the
permutation of litters to `L`. This condition means that the pointwise image of a near-litter `N`
under the permutation of atoms is a near-litter, and that the litter it is near to is just the image
of `Nᴸ` under the permutation of litters. It is easy to see that it is not necessary to include
the litter permutation in this definition, because the image of some litter `L` under the
permutation of litters must be the unique litter near the pointwise image of `Lᴬ` under the map of
atoms; we simply include the data of this extra permutation for definitional convenience. -/
structure BasePerm where
  atoms : Perm Atom
  litters : Perm Litter
  apply_near_apply (s : Set Atom) (L : Litter) : s ~ Lᴬ → atoms '' s ~ (litters L)ᴬ

namespace BasePerm

/-- If `π` is a base permutation, we write `πᴬ` for its associated permutation of atoms. -/
instance : SuperA BasePerm (Perm Atom) where
  superA := atoms

/-- If `π` is a base permutation, we write `πᴸ` for its associated permutation of litters. -/
instance : SuperL BasePerm (Perm Litter) where
  superL := litters

/-- For a base permutation `π` and an atom `a`, we write `π • a` for `πᴬ a`.
We will later show that this is a group action. -/
instance : SMul BasePerm Atom where
  smul π a := πᴬ a

/-- For a base permutation `π` and a litter `L`, we write `π • L` for `πᴸ L`.
We will later show that this is a group action. -/
instance : SMul BasePerm Litter where
  smul π L := πᴸ L

/-- A restatement of `apply_near_apply` using the new notations. -/
theorem smul_near_smul (π : BasePerm) (s : Set Atom) (L : Litter) :
    s ~ Lᴬ → π • s ~ (π • L)ᴬ :=
  π.apply_near_apply s L

/-- For a base permutation `π` and an atom `N`, we write `π • N` for the near-litter `N'` such that
`N'ᴸ = π • Nᴸ` and `N'ᴬ = π • Nᴬ`, where the latter group action on sets of atoms is the pointwise
action. We will later show that this is a group action. -/
instance : SMul BasePerm NearLitter where
  smul π N := ⟨π • Nᴸ, π • Nᴬ, π.smul_near_smul Nᴬ Nᴸ N.atoms_near_litter⟩

/-! We establish some useful definitional equalities. -/

theorem smul_atom_def (π : BasePerm) (a : Atom) :
    π • a = πᴬ a :=
  rfl

theorem smul_litter_def (π : BasePerm) (L : Litter) :
    π • L = πᴸ L :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem smul_nearLitter_atoms (π : BasePerm) (N : NearLitter) :
    (π • N)ᴬ = π • Nᴬ :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem smul_nearLitter_litter (π : BasePerm) (N : NearLitter) :
    (π • N)ᴸ = π • Nᴸ :=
  rfl

/-- An extensionality principle for base permutations: if two base permutations have the same
action on atoms, then they coincide. This is because we can recover the data of `πᴸ` from `πᴬ`,
given that `π` is a base permutation. -/
@[ext]
theorem ext {π₁ π₂ : BasePerm} (h : ∀ a : Atom, π₁ • a = π₂ • a) :
    π₁ = π₂ := by
  obtain ⟨πa₁, πl₁, h₁⟩ := π₁
  obtain ⟨πa₂, πl₂, h₂⟩ := π₂
  rw [mk.injEq]
  have : πa₁ = πa₂ := by ext a; exact h a
  refine ⟨this, ?_⟩
  ext L
  have h₁' := h₁ Lᴬ L near_rfl
  have h₂' := h₂ Lᴬ L near_rfl
  rw [this] at h₁'
  exact litter_eq_of_near <| near_trans (near_symm h₁') h₂'

/-!
## Group structure
-/

/-- The identity permutation. -/
instance : One BasePerm where
  one := ⟨1, 1, λ s L h ↦ by simpa only [Perm.coe_one, id_eq, Set.image_id']⟩

@[simp]
theorem one_atom :
    (1 : BasePerm)ᴬ = 1 :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem one_litter :
    (1 : BasePerm)ᴸ = 1 :=
  rfl

/-- The composition of permutations. -/
instance : Mul BasePerm where
  mul π₁ π₂ := ⟨π₁ᴬ * π₂ᴬ, π₁ᴸ * π₂ᴸ, λ s L h ↦ by
    have := π₁.smul_near_smul _ _ <| π₂.smul_near_smul s L h
    simpa only [Set.smul_set_def, Set.image_image] using this⟩

@[simp]
theorem mul_atom (π₁ π₂ : BasePerm) :
    (π₁ * π₂)ᴬ = π₁ᴬ * π₂ᴬ :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem mul_litter (π₁ π₂ : BasePerm) :
    (π₁ * π₂)ᴸ = π₁ᴸ * π₂ᴸ :=
  rfl

/-- The relevant instance of `smul_near_smul` for the inverse of a base permutation. -/
theorem inv_smul_near_inv_smul (π : BasePerm) (s : Set Atom) (L : Litter) :
    s ~ Lᴬ → πᴬ⁻¹ • s ~ (πᴸ⁻¹ • L)ᴬ := by
  intro h
  apply near_trans (near_image h ↑πᴬ⁻¹)
  have := π.smul_near_smul (πᴸ⁻¹ L)ᴬ (πᴸ⁻¹ L) near_rfl
  have := near_image this ↑πᴬ⁻¹
  simp only [smul_litter_def, smul_atom_def, Perm.apply_inv_self, Set.smul_set_def,
    Perm.image_inv, preimage_image] at this
  rw [Perm.image_inv]
  exact near_symm this

/-- The inverse of a permutation. -/
instance : Inv BasePerm where
  inv π := ⟨πᴬ⁻¹, πᴸ⁻¹, π.inv_smul_near_inv_smul⟩

@[simp]
theorem inv_atom (π : BasePerm) :
    π⁻¹ᴬ = πᴬ⁻¹ :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem inv_litter (π : BasePerm) :
    π⁻¹ᴸ = πᴸ⁻¹ :=
  rfl

/-- The group structure on base permutations. -/
instance : Group BasePerm where
  mul_assoc π₁ π₂ π₃ := by
    ext a
    simp only [smul_atom_def, mul_atom, mul_assoc]
  one_mul π := by
    ext a
    simp only [smul_atom_def, mul_atom, one_atom, one_mul]
  mul_one π := by
    ext a
    simp only [smul_atom_def, mul_atom, one_atom, mul_one]
  inv_mul_cancel π := by
    ext a
    simp only [smul_atom_def, mul_atom, inv_atom, inv_mul_cancel, Perm.coe_one, id_eq, one_atom]

/-- The action of base permutations on atoms is a group action. -/
instance : MulAction BasePerm Atom where
  one_smul _ := rfl
  mul_smul _ _ _ := rfl

/-- The action of base permutations on litters is a group action. -/
instance : MulAction BasePerm Litter where
  one_smul _ := by exact?

C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

import Mathlib.Logic.Equiv.Defs
import ConNF.Base.NearLitter

/-!
# Base permutations

In this file, we define the group of *base permutations*, and their actions on atoms, litters, and
near-litters. In the paper, these are called *`-1`-allowable permutations*, but that term has a
different meaning in this formalisation.
-/

universe u

open Cardinal Equiv
open scoped Pointwise

namespace ConNF

variable [Params.{u}]

/-!
## Definitions
-/

/-- A *base permutation* consists of a permutation of atoms, a permutation of litters, and a proof
that if some set `s` is near the litter set of some litter `L`, then when we apply the permutation
of atoms pointwise to `s`, the resulting set of atoms is near the litter obtained by applying the
permutation of litters to `L`. This condition means that the pointwise image of a near-litter `N`
under the permutation of atoms is a near-litter, and that the litter it is near to is just the image
of `Nᴸ` under the permutation of litters. It is easy to see that it is not necessary to include
the litter permutation in this definition, because the image of some litter `L` under the
permutation of litters must be the unique litter near the pointwise image of `Lᴬ` under the map of
atoms; we simply include the data of this extra permutation for definitional convenience. -/
structure BasePerm where
  atoms : Perm Atom
  litters : Perm Litter
  apply_near_apply (s : Set Atom) (L : Litter) : s ~ Lᴬ → atoms '' s ~ (litters L)ᴬ

namespace BasePerm

/-- If `π` is a base permutation, we write `πᴬ` for its associated permutation of atoms. -/
instance : SuperA BasePerm (Perm Atom) where
  superA := atoms

/-- If `π` is a base permutation, we write `πᴸ` for its associated permutation of litters. -/
instance : SuperL BasePerm (Perm Litter) where
  superL := litters

/-- For a base permutation `π` and an atom `a`, we write `π • a` for `πᴬ a`.
We will later show that this is a group action. -/
instance : SMul BasePerm Atom where
  smul π a := πᴬ a

/-- For a base permutation `π` and a litter `L`, we write `π • L` for `πᴸ L`.
We will later show that this is a group action. -/
instance : SMul BasePerm Litter where
  smul π L := πᴸ L

different meaning in this formalisation.

permutation of litters must be the unique litter near the pointwise image of `Lᴬ` under the map of
atoms; we simply include the data of this extra permutation for definitional convenience. -/

  atoms : Perm Atom
  litters : Perm Litter

C1_dependencies.name: rfl
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

content_full:
import Mathlib.Logic.Equiv.Defs
import ConNF.Base.NearLitter

/-!
# Base permutations

In this file, we define the group of *base permutations*, and their actions on atoms, litters, and
near-litters. In the paper, these are called *`-1`-allowable permutations*, but that term has a
different meaning in this formalisation.
-/

universe u

open Cardinal Equiv
open scoped Pointwise

namespace ConNF

variable [Params.{u}]

/-!
## Definitions
-/

/-- A *base permutation* consists of a permutation of atoms, a permutation of litters, and a proof
that if some set `s` is near the litter set of some litter `L`, then when we apply the permutation
of atoms pointwise to `s`, the resulting set of atoms is near the litter obtained by applying the
permutation of litters to `L`. This condition means that the pointwise image of a near-litter `N`
under the permutation of atoms is a near-litter, and that the litter it is near to is just the image
of `Nᴸ` under the permutation of litters. It is easy to see that it is not necessary to include
the litter permutation in this definition, because the image of some litter `L` under the
permutation of litters must be the unique litter near the pointwise image of `Lᴬ` under the map of
atoms; we simply include the data of this extra permutation for definitional convenience. -/
structure BasePerm where
  atoms : Perm Atom
  litters : Perm Litter
  apply_near_apply (s : Set Atom) (L : Litter) : s ~ Lᴬ → atoms '' s ~ (litters L)ᴬ

namespace BasePerm

/-- If `π` is a base permutation, we write `πᴬ` for its associated permutation of atoms. -/
instance : SuperA BasePerm (Perm Atom) where
  superA := atoms

/-- If `π` is a base permutation, we write `πᴸ` for its associated permutation of litters. -/
instance : SuperL BasePerm (Perm Litter) where
  superL := litters

/-- For a base permutation `π` and an atom `a`, we write `π • a` for `πᴬ a`.
We will later show that this is a group action. -/
instance : SMul BasePerm Atom where
  smul π a := πᴬ a

/-- For a base permutation `π` and a litter `L`, we write `π • L` for `πᴸ L`.
We will later show that this is a group action. -/
instance : SMul BasePerm Litter where
  smul π L := πᴸ L

/-- A restatement of `apply_near_apply` using the new notations. -/
theorem smul_near_smul (π : BasePerm) (s : Set Atom) (L : Litter) :
    s ~ Lᴬ → π • s ~ (π • L)ᴬ :=
  π.apply_near_apply s L

/-- For a base permutation `π` and an atom `N`, we write `π • N` for the near-litter `N'` such that
`N'ᴸ = π • Nᴸ` and `N'ᴬ = π • Nᴬ`, where the latter group action on sets of atoms is the pointwise
action. We will later show that this is a group action. -/
instance : SMul BasePerm NearLitter where
  smul π N := ⟨π • Nᴸ, π • Nᴬ, π.smul_near_smul Nᴬ Nᴸ N.atoms_near_litter⟩

/-! We establish some useful definitional equalities. -/

theorem smul_atom_def (π : BasePerm) (a : Atom) :
    π • a = πᴬ a :=
  rfl

theorem smul_litter_def (π : BasePerm) (L : Litter) :
    π • L = πᴸ L :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem smul_nearLitter_atoms (π : BasePerm) (N : NearLitter) :
    (π • N)ᴬ = π • Nᴬ :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem smul_nearLitter_litter (π : BasePerm) (N : NearLitter) :
    (π • N)ᴸ = π • Nᴸ :=
  rfl

/-- An extensionality principle for base permutations: if two base permutations have the same
action on atoms, then they coincide. This is because we can recover the data of `πᴸ` from `πᴬ`,
given that `π` is a base permutation. -/
@[ext]
theorem ext {π₁ π₂ : BasePerm} (h : ∀ a : Atom, π₁ • a = π₂ • a) :
    π₁ = π₂ := by
  obtain ⟨πa₁, πl₁, h₁⟩ := π₁
  obtain ⟨πa₂, πl₂, h₂⟩ := π₂
  rw [mk.injEq]
  have : πa₁ = πa₂ := by ext a; exact h a
  refine ⟨this, ?_⟩
  ext L
  have h₁' := h₁ Lᴬ L near_rfl
  have h₂' := h₂ Lᴬ L near_rfl
  rw [this] at h₁'
  exact litter_eq_of_near <| near_trans (near_symm h₁') h₂'

/-!
## Group structure
-/

/-- The identity permutation. -/
instance : One BasePerm where
  one := ⟨1, 1, λ s L h ↦ by simpa only [Perm.coe_one, id_eq, Set.image_id']⟩

@[simp]
theorem one_atom :
    (1 : BasePerm)ᴬ = 1 :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem one_litter :
    (1 : BasePerm)ᴸ = 1 :=
  rfl

/-- The composition of permutations. -/
instance : Mul BasePerm where
  mul π₁ π₂ := ⟨π₁ᴬ * π₂ᴬ, π₁ᴸ * π₂ᴸ, λ s L h ↦ by
    have := π₁.smul_near_smul _ _ <| π₂.smul_near_smul s L h
    simpa only [Set.smul_set_def, Set.image_image] using this⟩

@[simp]
theorem mul_atom (π₁ π₂ : BasePerm) :
    (π₁ * π₂)ᴬ = π₁ᴬ * π₂ᴬ :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem mul_litter (π₁ π₂ : BasePerm) :
    (π₁ * π₂)ᴸ = π₁ᴸ * π₂ᴸ :=
  rfl

/-- The relevant instance of `smul_near_smul` for the inverse of a base permutation. -/
theorem inv_smul_near_inv_smul (π : BasePerm) (s : Set Atom) (L : Litter) :
    s ~ Lᴬ → πᴬ⁻¹ • s ~ (πᴸ⁻¹ • L)ᴬ := by
  intro h
  apply near_trans (near_image h ↑πᴬ⁻¹)
  have := π.smul_near_smul (πᴸ⁻¹ L)ᴬ (πᴸ⁻¹ L) near_rfl
  have := near_image this ↑πᴬ⁻¹
  simp only [smul_litter_def, smul_atom_def, Perm.apply_inv_self, Set.smul_set_def,
    Perm.image_inv, preimage_image] at this
  rw [Perm.image_inv]
  exact near_symm this

/-- The inverse of a permutation. -/
instance : Inv BasePerm where
  inv π := ⟨πᴬ⁻¹, πᴸ⁻¹, π.inv_smul_near_inv_smul⟩

@[simp]
theorem inv_atom (π : BasePerm) :
    π⁻¹ᴬ = πᴬ⁻¹ :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem inv_litter (π : BasePerm) :
    π⁻¹ᴸ = πᴸ⁻¹ :=
  rfl

/-- The group structure on base permutations. -/
instance : Group BasePerm where
  mul_assoc π₁ π₂ π₃ := by
    ext a
    simp only [smul_atom_def, mul_atom, mul_assoc]
  one_mul π := by
    ext a
    simp only [smul_atom_def, mul_atom, one_atom, one_mul]
  mul_one π := by
    ext a
    simp only [smul_atom_def, mul_atom, one_atom, mul_one]
  inv_mul_cancel π := by
    ext a
    simp only [smul_atom_def, mul_atom, inv_atom, inv_mul_cancel, Perm.coe_one, id_eq, one_atom]

permutation of litters to `L`. This condition means that the pointwise image of a near-litter `N`

C1_dependencies.name: rfl
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

that if some set `s` is near the litter set of some litter `L`, then when we apply the permutation
of atoms pointwise to `s`, the resulting set of atoms is near the litter obtained by applying the
permutation of litters to `L`. This condition means that the pointwise image of a near-litter `N`
under the permutation of atoms is a near-litter, and that the litter it is near to is just the image

the litter permutation in this definition, because the image of some litter `L` under the
permutation of litters must be the unique litter near the pointwise image of `Lᴬ` under the map of
atoms; we simply include the data of this extra permutation for definitional convenience. -/

  atoms : Perm Atom
  litters : Perm Litter

import ConNF.Base.NearLitter

# Base permutations

In this file, we define the group of *base permutations*, and their actions on atoms, litters, and
near-litters. In the paper, these are called *`-1`-allowable permutations*, but that term has a
different meaning in this formalisation.
-/

universe u

open Cardinal Equiv
open scoped Pointwise

namespace ConNF

variable [Params.{u}]

/-!
## Definitions
-/

/-- A *base permutation* consists of a permutation of atoms, a permutation of litters, and a proof
that if some set `s` is near the litter set of some litter `L`, then when we apply the permutation
of atoms pointwise to `s`, the resulting set of atoms is near the litter obtained by applying the
permutation of litters to `L`. This condition means that the pointwise image of a near-litter `N`
under the permutation of atoms is a near-litter, and that the litter it is near to is just the image
of `Nᴸ` under the permutation of litters. It is easy to see that it is not necessary to include
the litter permutation in this definition, because the image of some litter `L` under the
permutation of litters must be the unique litter near the pointwise image of `Lᴬ` under the map of
atoms; we simply include the data of this extra permutation for definitional convenience. -/
structure BasePerm where
  atoms : Perm Atom
  litters : Perm Litter
  apply_near_apply (s : Set Atom) (L : Litter) : s ~ Lᴬ → atoms '' s ~ (litters L)ᴬ

namespace BasePerm

/-- If `π` is a base permutation, we write `πᴬ` for its associated permutation of atoms. -/
instance : SuperA BasePerm (Perm Atom) where
  superA := atoms

/-- If `π` is a base permutation, we write `πᴸ` for its associated permutation of litters. -/
instance : SuperL BasePerm (Perm Litter) where
  superL := litters

/-- For a base permutation `π` and an atom `a`, we write `π • a` for `πᴬ a`.
We will later show that this is a group action. -/
instance : SMul BasePerm Atom where
  smul π a := πᴬ a

/-- For a base permutation `π` and a litter `L`, we write `π • L` for `πᴸ L`.
We will later show that this is a group action. -/
instance : SMul BasePerm Litter where
  smul π L := πᴸ L

/-- A restatement of `apply_near_apply` using the new notations. -/
theorem smul_near_smul (π : BasePerm) (s : Set Atom) (L : Litter) :
    s ~ Lᴬ → π • s ~ (π • L)ᴬ :=
  π.apply_near_apply s L

/-- For a base permutation `π` and an atom `N`, we write `π • N` for the near-litter `N'` such that
`N'ᴸ = π • Nᴸ` and `N'ᴬ = π • Nᴬ`, where the latter group action on sets of atoms is the pointwise

instance : SMul BasePerm NearLitter where
  smul π N := ⟨π • Nᴸ, π • Nᴬ, π.smul_near_smul Nᴬ Nᴸ N.atoms_near_litter⟩

/-! We establish some useful definitional equalities. -/

theorem smul_atom_def (π : BasePerm) (a : Atom) :
    π • a = πᴬ a :=
  rfl

theorem smul_litter_def (π : BasePerm) (L : Litter) :
    π • L = πᴸ L :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem smul_nearLitter_atoms (π : BasePerm) (N : NearLitter) :
    (π • N)ᴬ = π • Nᴬ :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem smul_nearLitter_litter (π : BasePerm) (N : NearLitter) :
    (π • N)ᴸ = π • Nᴸ :=
  rfl

action on atoms, then they coincide. This is because we can recover the data of `πᴸ` from `πᴬ`,

    π₁ = π₂ := by
  obtain ⟨πa₁, πl₁, h₁⟩ := π₁
  obtain ⟨πa₂, πl₂, h₂⟩ := π₂

  rfl

    (π₁ * π₂)ᴸ = π₁ᴸ * π₂ᴸ :=
  rfl

theorem inv_smul_near_inv_smul (π : BasePerm) (s : Set Atom) (L : Litter) :
    s ~ Lᴬ → πᴬ⁻¹ • s ~ (πᴸ⁻¹ • L)ᴬ := by

  inv π := ⟨πᴬ⁻¹, πᴸ⁻¹, π.inv_smul_near_inv_smul⟩

C1_dependencies.name: rfl
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

import Mathlib.Logic.Equiv.Defs
import ConNF.Base.NearLitter

/-!
# Base permutations

In this file, we define the group of *base permutations*, and their actions on atoms, litters, and
near-litters. In the paper, these are called *`-1`-allowable permutations*, but that term has a
different meaning in this formalisation.
-/

universe u

open Cardinal Equiv
open scoped Pointwise

namespace ConNF

variable [Params.{u}]

/-!
## Definitions
-/

/-- A *base permutation* consists of a permutation of atoms, a permutation of litters, and a proof
that if some set `s` is near the litter set of some litter `L`, then when we apply the permutation
of atoms pointwise to `s`, the resulting set of atoms is near the litter obtained by applying the
permutation of litters to `L`. This condition means that the pointwise image of a near-litter `N`
under the permutation of atoms is a near-litter, and that the litter it is near to is just the image
of `Nᴸ` under the permutation of litters. It is easy to see that it is not necessary to include
the litter permutation in this definition, because the image of some litter `L` under the
permutation of litters must be the unique litter near the pointwise image of `Lᴬ` under the map of
atoms; we simply include the data of this extra permutation for definitional convenience. -/
structure BasePerm where
  atoms : Perm Atom
  litters : Perm Litter
  apply_near_apply (s : Set Atom) (L : Litter) : s ~ Lᴬ → atoms '' s ~ (litters L)ᴬ

namespace BasePerm

/-- If `π` is a base permutation, we write `πᴬ` for its associated permutation of atoms. -/
instance : SuperA BasePerm (Perm Atom) where
  superA := atoms

/-- If `π` is a base permutation, we write `πᴸ` for its associated permutation of litters. -/
instance : SuperL BasePerm (Perm Litter) where
  superL := litters

/-- For a base permutation `π` and an atom `a`, we write `π • a` for `πᴬ a`.
We will later show that this is a group action. -/
instance : SMul BasePerm Atom where
  smul π a := πᴬ a

/-- For a base permutation `π` and a litter `L`, we write `π • L` for `πᴸ L`.
We will later show that this is a group action. -/
instance : SMul BasePerm Litter where
  smul π L := πᴸ L

/-- A restatement of `apply_near_apply` using the new notations. -/
theorem smul_near_smul (π : BasePerm) (s : Set Atom) (L : Litter) :
    s ~ Lᴬ → π • s ~ (π • L)ᴬ :=
  π.apply_near_apply s L

/-- For a base permutation `π` and an atom `N`, we write `π • N` for the near-litter `N'` such that
`N'ᴸ = π • Nᴸ` and `N'ᴬ = π • Nᴬ`, where the latter group action on sets of atoms is the pointwise
action. We will later show that this is a group action. -/
instance : SMul BasePerm NearLitter where
  smul π N := ⟨π • Nᴸ, π • Nᴬ, π.smul_near_smul Nᴬ Nᴸ N.atoms_near_litter⟩

theorem smul_atom_def (π : BasePerm) (a : Atom) :
    π • a = πᴬ a :=
  rfl

theorem smul_litter_def (π : BasePerm) (L : Litter) :
    π • L = πᴸ L :=
  rfl

    (π • N)ᴬ = π • Nᴬ :=

action on atoms, then they coincide. This is because we can recover the data of `πᴸ` from `πᴬ`,
given that `π` is a base permutation. -/
@[ext]
theorem ext {π₁ π₂ : BasePerm} (h : ∀ a : Atom, π₁ • a = π₂ • a) :
    π₁ = π₂ := by
  obtain ⟨πa₁, πl₁, h₁⟩ := π₁
  obtain ⟨πa₂, πl₂, h₂⟩ := π₂

import Mathlib.Logic.Equiv.Defs
import ConNF.Base.NearLitter

/-!
# Base permutations

In this file, we define the group of *base permutations*, and their actions on atoms, litters, and
near-litters. In the paper, these are called *`-1`-allowable permutations*, but that term has a
different meaning in this formalisation.
-/

universe u

open Cardinal Equiv
open scoped Pointwise

namespace ConNF

variable [Params.{u}]

/-!
## Definitions
-/

/-- A *base permutation* consists of a permutation of atoms, a permutation of litters, and a proof
that if some set `s` is near the litter set of some litter `L`, then when we apply the permutation
of atoms pointwise to `s`, the resulting set of atoms is near the litter obtained by applying the
permutation of litters to `L`. This condition means that the pointwise image of a near-litter `N`
under the permutation of atoms is a near-litter, and that the litter it is near to is just the image
of `Nᴸ` under the permutation of litters. It is easy to see that it is not necessary to include
the litter permutation in this definition, because the image of some litter `L` under the
permutation of litters must be the unique litter near the pointwise image of `Lᴬ` under the map of
atoms; we simply include the data of this extra permutation for definitional convenience. -/
structure BasePerm where
  atoms : Perm Atom
  litters : Perm Litter
  apply_near_apply (s : Set Atom) (L : Litter) : s ~ Lᴬ → atoms '' s ~ (litters L)ᴬ

namespace BasePerm

/-- If `π` is a base permutation, we write `πᴬ` for its associated permutation of atoms. -/
instance : SuperA BasePerm (Perm Atom) where
  superA := atoms

/-- If `π` is a base permutation, we write `πᴸ` for its associated permutation of litters. -/
instance : SuperL BasePerm (Perm Litter) where
  superL := litters

/-- For a base permutation `π` and an atom `a`, we write `π • a` for `πᴬ a`.
We will later show that this is a group action. -/
instance : SMul BasePerm Atom where
  smul π a := πᴬ a

/-- For a base permutation `π` and a litter `L`, we write `π • L` for `πᴸ L`.
We will later show that this is a group action. -/
instance : SMul BasePerm Litter where
  smul π L := πᴸ L

/-- A restatement of `apply_near_apply` using the new notations. -/
theorem smul_near_smul (π : BasePerm) (s : Set Atom) (L : Litter) :
    s ~ Lᴬ → π • s ~ (π • L)ᴬ :=
  π.apply_near_apply s L

/-- For a base permutation `π` and an atom `N`, we write `π • N` for the near-litter `N'` such that
`N'ᴸ = π • Nᴸ` and `N'ᴬ = π • Nᴬ`, where the latter group action on sets of atoms is the pointwise
action. We will later show that this is a group action. -/
instance : SMul BasePerm NearLitter where
  smul π N := ⟨π • Nᴸ, π • Nᴬ, π.smul_near_smul Nᴬ Nᴸ N.atoms_near_litter⟩

/-! We establish some useful definitional equalities. -/

theorem smul_atom_def (π : BasePerm) (a : Atom) :
    π • a = πᴬ a :=
  rfl

theorem smul_litter_def (π : BasePerm) (L : Litter) :
    π • L = πᴸ L :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem smul_nearLitter_atoms (π : BasePerm) (N : NearLitter) :
    (π • N)ᴬ = π • Nᴬ :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem smul_nearLitter_litter (π : BasePerm) (N : NearLitter) :
    (π • N)ᴸ = π • Nᴸ :=
  rfl

/-- An extensionality principle for base permutations: if two base permutations have the same
action on atoms, then they coincide. This is because we can recover the data of `πᴸ` from `πᴬ`,
given that `π` is a base permutation. -/
@[ext]
theorem ext {π₁ π₂ : BasePerm} (h : ∀ a : Atom, π₁ • a = π₂ • a) :
    π₁ = π₂ := by
  obtain ⟨πa₁, πl₁, h₁⟩ := π₁
  obtain ⟨πa₂, πl₂, h₂⟩ := π₂
  rw [mk.injEq]
  have : πa₁ = πa₂ := by ext a; exact h a
  refine ⟨this, ?_⟩
  ext L
  have h₁' := h₁ Lᴬ L near_rfl
  have h₂' := h₂ Lᴬ L near_rfl
  rw [this] at h₁'
  exact litter_eq_of_near <| near_trans (near_symm h₁') h₂'

/-!
## Group structure
-/

/-- The identity permutation. -/
instance : One BasePerm where
  one := ⟨1, 1, λ s L h ↦ by simpa only [Perm.coe_one, id_eq, Set.image_id']⟩

@[simp]
theorem one_atom :
    (1 : BasePerm)ᴬ = 1 :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem one_litter :
    (1 : BasePerm)ᴸ = 1 :=
  rfl

/-- The composition of permutations. -/
instance : Mul BasePerm where
  mul π₁ π₂ := ⟨π₁ᴬ * π₂ᴬ, π₁ᴸ * π₂ᴸ, λ s L h ↦ by
    have := π₁.smul_near_smul _ _ <| π₂.smul_near_smul s L h
    simpa only [Set.smul_set_def, Set.image_image] using this⟩

@[simp]
theorem mul_atom (π₁ π₂ : BasePerm) :
    (π₁ * π₂)ᴬ = π₁ᴬ * π₂ᴬ :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem mul_litter (π₁ π₂ : BasePerm) :
    (π₁ * π₂)ᴸ = π₁ᴸ * π₂ᴸ :=
  rfl

/-- The relevant instance of `smul_near_smul` for the inverse of a base permutation. -/
theorem inv_smul_near_inv_smul (π : BasePerm) (s : Set Atom) (L : Litter) :
    s ~ Lᴬ → πᴬ⁻¹ • s ~ (πᴸ⁻¹ • L)ᴬ := by
  intro h
  apply near_trans (near_image h ↑πᴬ⁻¹)
  have := π.smul_near_smul (πᴸ⁻¹ L)ᴬ (πᴸ⁻¹ L) near_rfl
  have := near_image this ↑πᴬ⁻¹
  simp only [smul_litter_def, smul_atom_def, Perm.apply_inv_self, Set.smul_set_def,
    Perm.image_inv, preimage_image] at this
  rw [Perm.image_inv]
  exact near_symm this

/-- The inverse of a permutation. -/
instance : Inv BasePerm where
  inv π := ⟨πᴬ⁻¹, πᴸ⁻¹, π.inv_smul_near_inv_smul⟩
annotation:

  inv π := ⟨πᴬ⁻¹, πᴸ⁻¹, π.inv_smul_near_inv_smul⟩

import Mathlib.Logic.Equiv.Defs

/-!
# Base permutations

In this file, we define the group of *base permutations*, and their actions on atoms, litters, and
near-litters. In the paper, these are called *`-1`-allowable permutations*, but that term has a
different meaning in this formalisation.
-/

universe u

open Cardinal Equiv
open scoped Pointwise

namespace ConNF

variable [Params.{u}]

/-!
## Definitions
-/

/-- A *base permutation* consists of a permutation of atoms, a permutation of litters, and a proof
that if some set `s` is near the litter set of some litter `L`, then when we apply the permutation
of atoms pointwise to `s`, the resulting set of atoms is near the litter obtained by applying the
permutation of litters to `L`. This condition means that the pointwise image of a near-litter `N`
under the permutation of atoms is a near-litter, and that the litter it is near to is just the image
of `Nᴸ` under the permutation of litters. It is easy to see that it is not necessary to include
the litter permutation in this definition, because the image of some litter `L` under the
permutation of litters must be the unique litter near the pointwise image of `Lᴬ` under the map of
atoms; we simply include the data of this extra permutation for definitional convenience. -/
structure BasePerm where
  atoms : Perm Atom
  litters : Perm Litter
  apply_near_apply (s : Set Atom) (L : Litter) : s ~ Lᴬ → atoms '' s ~ (litters L)ᴬ

namespace BasePerm

/-- If `π` is a base permutation, we write `πᴬ` for its associated permutation of atoms. -/
instance : SuperA BasePerm (Perm Atom) where
  superA := atoms

/-- If `π` is a base permutation, we write `πᴸ` for its associated permutation of litters. -/
instance : SuperL BasePerm (Perm Litter) where
  superL := litters

/-- For a base permutation `π` and an atom `a`, we write `π • a` for `πᴬ a`.
We will later show that this is a group action. -/
instance : SMul BasePerm Atom where
  smul π a := πᴬ a

/-- For a base permutation `π` and a litter `L`, we write `π • L` for `πᴸ L`.
We will later show that this is a group action. -/
instance : SMul BasePerm Litter where
  smul π L := πᴸ L

theorem smul_near_smul (π : BasePerm) (s : Set Atom) (L : Litter) :
    s ~ Lᴬ → π • s ~ (π • L)ᴬ :=
  π.apply_near_apply s L

`N'ᴸ = π • Nᴸ` and `N'ᴬ = π • Nᴬ`, where the latter group action on sets of atoms is the pointwise

  rfl

  rfl

  rfl

@[simp]

import Mathlib.Logic.Equiv.Defs
import ConNF.Base.NearLitter

/-!
# Base permutations

In this file, we define the group of *base permutations*, and their actions on atoms, litters, and
near-litters. In the paper, these are called *`-1`-allowable permutations*, but that term has a
different meaning in this formalisation.
-/

universe u

open Cardinal Equiv
open scoped Pointwise

namespace ConNF

variable [Params.{u}]

/-!
## Definitions
-/

/-- A *base permutation* consists of a permutation of atoms, a permutation of litters, and a proof
that if some set `s` is near the litter set of some litter `L`, then when we apply the permutation
of atoms pointwise to `s`, the resulting set of atoms is near the litter obtained by applying the
permutation of litters to `L`. This condition means that the pointwise image of a near-litter `N`
under the permutation of atoms is a near-litter, and that the litter it is near to is just the image
of `Nᴸ` under the permutation of litters. It is easy to see that it is not necessary to include
the litter permutation in this definition, because the image of some litter `L` under the
permutation of litters must be the unique litter near the pointwise image of `Lᴬ` under the map of
atoms; we simply include the data of this extra permutation for definitional convenience. -/
structure BasePerm where
  atoms : Perm Atom
  litters : Perm Litter
  apply_near_apply (s : Set Atom) (L : Litter) : s ~ Lᴬ → atoms '' s ~ (litters L)ᴬ

namespace BasePerm

/-- If `π` is a base permutation, we write `πᴬ` for its associated permutation of atoms. -/
instance : SuperA BasePerm (Perm Atom) where
  superA := atoms

/-- If `π` is a base permutation, we write `πᴸ` for its associated permutation of litters. -/
instance : SuperL BasePerm (Perm Litter) where
  superL := litters

/-- For a base permutation `π` and an atom `a`, we write `π • a` for `πᴬ a`.
We will later show that this is a group action. -/
instance : SMul BasePerm Atom where
  smul π a := πᴬ a

/-- For a base permutation `π` and a litter `L`, we write `π • L` for `πᴸ L`.
We will later show that this is a group action. -/
instance : SMul BasePerm Litter where
  smul π L := πᴸ L

/-- A restatement of `apply_near_apply` using the new notations. -/
theorem smul_near_smul (π : BasePerm) (s : Set Atom) (L : Litter) :
    s ~ Lᴬ → π • s ~ (π • L)ᴬ :=
  π.apply_near_apply s L

/-- For a base permutation `π` and an atom `N`, we write `π • N` for the near-litter `N'` such that
`N'ᴸ = π • Nᴸ` and `N'ᴬ = π • Nᴬ`, where the latter group action on sets of atoms is the pointwise
action. We will later show that this is a group action. -/
instance : SMul BasePerm NearLitter where
  smul π N := ⟨π • Nᴸ, π • Nᴬ, π.smul_near_smul Nᴬ Nᴸ N.atoms_near_litter⟩

/-! We establish some useful definitional equalities. -/

theorem smul_atom_def (π : BasePerm) (a : Atom) :
    π • a = πᴬ a :=
  rfl

theorem smul_litter_def (π : BasePerm) (L : Litter) :
    π • L = πᴸ L :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem smul_nearLitter_atoms (π : BasePerm) (N : NearLitter) :
    (π • N)ᴬ = π • Nᴬ :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem smul_nearLitter_litter (π : BasePerm) (N : NearLitter) :
    (π • N)ᴸ = π • Nᴸ :=
  rfl

/-- An extensionality principle for base permutations: if two base permutations have the same
action on atoms, then they coincide. This is because we can recover the data of `πᴸ` from `πᴬ`,
given that `π` is a base permutation. -/
@[ext]
theorem ext {π₁ π₂ : BasePerm} (h : ∀ a : Atom, π₁ • a = π₂ • a) :
    π₁ = π₂ := by
  obtain ⟨πa₁, πl₁, h₁⟩ := π₁
  obtain ⟨πa₂, πl₂, h₂⟩ := π₂
  rw [mk.injEq]
  have : πa₁ = πa₂ := by ext a; exact h a
  refine ⟨this, ?_⟩
  ext L
  have h₁' := h₁ Lᴬ L near_rfl
  have h₂' := h₂ Lᴬ L near_rfl
  rw [this] at h₁'
  exact litter_eq_of_near <| near_trans (near_symm h₁') h₂'

/-!
## Group structure
-/

/-- The identity permutation. -/
instance : One BasePerm where
  one := ⟨1, 1, λ s L h ↦ by simpa only [Perm.coe_one, id_eq, Set.image_id']⟩

@[simp]
theorem one_atom :
    (1 : BasePerm)ᴬ = 1 :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem one_litter :
    (1 : BasePerm)ᴸ = 1 :=
  rfl

/-- The composition of permutations. -/
instance : Mul BasePerm where
  mul π₁ π₂ := ⟨π₁ᴬ * π₂ᴬ, π₁ᴸ * π₂ᴸ, λ s L h ↦ by
    have := π₁.smul_near_smul _ _ <| π₂.smul_near_smul s L h
    simpa only [Set.smul_set_def, Set.image_image] using this⟩

@[simp]
theorem mul_atom (π₁ π₂ : BasePerm) :
    (π₁ * π₂)ᴬ = π₁ᴬ * π₂ᴬ :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem mul_litter (π₁ π₂ : BasePerm) :
    (π₁ * π₂)ᴸ = π₁ᴸ * π₂ᴸ := by exact?

C1_dependencies.name: rfl
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

different meaning in this formalisation.

permutation of litters to `L`. This condition means that the pointwise image of a near-litter `N`
under the permutation of atoms is a near-litter, and that the litter it is near to is just the image
of `Nᴸ` under the permutation of litters. It is easy to see that it is not necessary to include
the litter permutation in this definition, because the image of some litter `L` under the
permutation of litters must be the unique litter near the pointwise image of `Lᴬ` under the map of

  atoms : Perm Atom
  litters : Perm Litter

C1_dependencies.name: rfl
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

import Mathlib.Logic.Equiv.Defs
import ConNF.Base.NearLitter

/-!
# Base permutations

In this file, we define the group of *base permutations*, and their actions on atoms, litters, and
near-litters. In the paper, these are called *`-1`-allowable permutations*, but that term has a
different meaning in this formalisation.
-/

universe u

open Cardinal Equiv
open scoped Pointwise

namespace ConNF

variable [Params.{u}]

/-!
## Definitions
-/

/-- A *base permutation* consists of a permutation of atoms, a permutation of litters, and a proof
that if some set `s` is near the litter set of some litter `L`, then when we apply the permutation
of atoms pointwise to `s`, the resulting set of atoms is near the litter obtained by applying the
permutation of litters to `L`. This condition means that the pointwise image of a near-litter `N`
under the permutation of atoms is a near-litter, and that the litter it is near to is just the image
of `Nᴸ` under the permutation of litters. It is easy to see that it is not necessary to include
the litter permutation in this definition, because the image of some litter `L` under the
permutation of litters must be the unique litter near the pointwise image of `Lᴬ` under the map of
atoms; we simply include the data of this extra permutation for definitional convenience. -/
structure BasePerm where
  atoms : Perm Atom
  litters : Perm Litter
  apply_near_apply (s : Set Atom) (L : Litter) : s ~ Lᴬ → atoms '' s ~ (litters L)ᴬ

namespace BasePerm

/-- If `π` is a base permutation, we write `πᴬ` for its associated permutation of atoms. -/
instance : SuperA BasePerm (Perm Atom) where
  superA := atoms

/-- If `π` is a base permutation, we write `πᴸ` for its associated permutation of litters. -/
instance : SuperL BasePerm (Perm Litter) where
  superL := litters

/-- For a base permutation `π` and an atom `a`, we write `π • a` for `πᴬ a`.
We will later show that this is a group action. -/
instance : SMul BasePerm Atom where
  smul π a := πᴬ a

/-- For a base permutation `π` and a litter `L`, we write `π • L` for `πᴸ L`.
We will later show that this is a group action. -/
instance : SMul BasePerm Litter where
  smul π L := πᴸ L

/-- A restatement of `apply_near_apply` using the new notations. -/
theorem smul_near_smul (π : BasePerm) (s : Set Atom) (L : Litter) :
    s ~ Lᴬ → π • s ~ (π • L)ᴬ :=
  π.apply_near_apply s L

/-- For a base permutation `π` and an atom `N`, we write `π • N` for the near-litter `N'` such that
`N'ᴸ = π • Nᴸ` and `N'ᴬ = π • Nᴬ`, where the latter group action on sets of atoms is the pointwise
action. We will later show that this is a group action. -/
instance : SMul BasePerm NearLitter where
  smul π N := ⟨π • Nᴸ, π • Nᴬ, π.smul_near_smul Nᴬ Nᴸ N.atoms_near_litter⟩

/-! We establish some useful definitional equalities. -/

theorem smul_atom_def (π : BasePerm) (a : Atom) :
    π • a = πᴬ a :=
  rfl

theorem smul_litter_def (π : BasePerm) (L : Litter) :
    π • L = πᴸ L :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem smul_nearLitter_atoms (π : BasePerm) (N : NearLitter) :
    (π • N)ᴬ = π • Nᴬ :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem smul_nearLitter_litter (π : BasePerm) (N : NearLitter) :
    (π • N)ᴸ = π • Nᴸ :=
  rfl

/-- An extensionality principle for base permutations: if two base permutations have the same
action on atoms, then they coincide. This is because we can recover the data of `πᴸ` from `πᴬ`,
given that `π` is a base permutation. -/
@[ext]
theorem ext {π₁ π₂ : BasePerm} (h : ∀ a : Atom, π₁ • a = π₂ • a) :
    π₁ = π₂ := by
  obtain ⟨πa₁, πl₁, h₁⟩ := π₁
  obtain ⟨πa₂, πl₂, h₂⟩ := π₂
  rw [mk.injEq]
  have : πa₁ = πa₂ := by ext a; exact h a
  refine ⟨this, ?_⟩

import Mathlib.Logic.Equiv.Defs
import ConNF.Base.NearLitter

/-!
# Base permutations

In this file, we define the group of *base permutations*, and their actions on atoms, litters, and
near-litters. In the paper, these are called *`-1`-allowable permutations*, but that term has a
different meaning in this formalisation.
-/

universe u

open Cardinal Equiv
open scoped Pointwise

namespace ConNF

variable [Params.{u}]

/-!
## Definitions
-/

/-- A *base permutation* consists of a permutation of atoms, a permutation of litters, and a proof
that if some set `s` is near the litter set of some litter `L`, then when we apply the permutation
of atoms pointwise to `s`, the resulting set of atoms is near the litter obtained by applying the
permutation of litters to `L`. This condition means that the pointwise image of a near-litter `N`
under the permutation of atoms is a near-litter, and that the litter it is near to is just the image
of `Nᴸ` under the permutation of litters. It is easy to see that it is not necessary to include
the litter permutation in this definition, because the image of some litter `L` under the
permutation of litters must be the unique litter near the pointwise image of `Lᴬ` under the map of
atoms; we simply include the data of this extra permutation for definitional convenience. -/
structure BasePerm where
  atoms : Perm Atom
  litters : Perm Litter
  apply_near_apply (s : Set Atom) (L : Litter) : s ~ Lᴬ → atoms '' s ~ (litters L)ᴬ

namespace BasePerm

/-- If `π` is a base permutation, we write `πᴬ` for its associated permutation of atoms. -/
instance : SuperA BasePerm (Perm Atom) where
  superA := atoms

/-- If `π` is a base permutation, we write `πᴸ` for its associated permutation of litters. -/
instance : SuperL BasePerm (Perm Litter) where
  superL := litters

/-- For a base permutation `π` and an atom `a`, we write `π • a` for `πᴬ a`.
We will later show that this is a group action. -/
instance : SMul BasePerm Atom where
  smul π a := πᴬ a

/-- For a base permutation `π` and a litter `L`, we write `π • L` for `πᴸ L`.
We will later show that this is a group action. -/
instance : SMul BasePerm Litter where
  smul π L := πᴸ L

/-- A restatement of `apply_near_apply` using the new notations. -/
theorem smul_near_smul (π : BasePerm) (s : Set Atom) (L : Litter) :
    s ~ Lᴬ → π • s ~ (π • L)ᴬ :=
  π.apply_near_apply s L

/-- For a base permutation `π` and an atom `N`, we write `π • N` for the near-litter `N'` such that
`N'ᴸ = π • Nᴸ` and `N'ᴬ = π • Nᴬ`, where the latter group action on sets of atoms is the pointwise
action. We will later show that this is a group action. -/
instance : SMul BasePerm NearLitter where
  smul π N := ⟨π • Nᴸ, π • Nᴬ, π.smul_near_smul Nᴬ Nᴸ N.atoms_near_litter⟩

/-! We establish some useful definitional equalities. -/

theorem smul_atom_def (π : BasePerm) (a : Atom) :
    π • a = πᴬ a :=
  rfl

theorem smul_litter_def (π : BasePerm) (L : Litter) :
    π • L = πᴸ L :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem smul_nearLitter_atoms (π : BasePerm) (N : NearLitter) :
    (π • N)ᴬ = π • Nᴬ :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem smul_nearLitter_litter (π : BasePerm) (N : NearLitter) :
    (π • N)ᴸ = π • Nᴸ :=
  rfl

/-- An extensionality principle for base permutations: if two base permutations have the same
action on atoms, then they coincide. This is because we can recover the data of `πᴸ` from `πᴬ`,
given that `π` is a base permutation. -/
@[ext]
theorem ext {π₁ π₂ : BasePerm} (h : ∀ a : Atom, π₁ • a = π₂ • a) :
    π₁ = π₂ := by
  obtain ⟨πa₁, πl₁, h₁⟩ := π₁
  obtain ⟨πa₂, πl₂, h₂⟩ := π₂
  rw [mk.injEq]
  have : πa₁ = πa₂ := by ext a; exact h a
  refine ⟨this, ?_⟩
  ext L
  have h₁' := h₁ Lᴬ L near_rfl
  have h₂' := h₂ Lᴬ L near_rfl
  rw [this] at h₁'
  exact litter_eq_of_near <| near_trans (near_symm h₁') h₂'

/-!
## Group structure
-/

/-- The identity permutation. -/
instance : One BasePerm where
  one := ⟨1, 1, λ s L h ↦ by simpa only [Perm.coe_one, id_eq, Set.image_id']⟩

@[simp]
theorem one_atom :
    (1 : BasePerm)ᴬ = 1 :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem one_litter :
    (1 : BasePerm)ᴸ = 1 :=
  rfl

/-- The composition of permutations. -/
instance : Mul BasePerm where
  mul π₁ π₂ := ⟨π₁ᴬ * π₂ᴬ, π₁ᴸ * π₂ᴸ, λ s L h ↦ by
    have := π₁.smul_near_smul _ _ <| π₂.smul_near_smul s L h
    simpa only [Set.smul_set_def, Set.image_image] using this⟩

C1_dependencies.name: rfl
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

action on atoms, then they coincide. This is because we can recover the data of `πᴸ` from `πᴬ`,

  have h₂' := h₂ Lᴬ L near_rfl
  rw [this] at h₁'
  exact litter_eq_of_near <| near_trans (near_symm h₁') h₂'

C1_dependencies.name: rfl
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

that if some set `s` is near the litter set of some litter `L`, then when we apply the permutation

  atoms : Perm Atom
  litters : Perm Litter
  apply_near_apply (s : Set Atom) (L : Litter) : s ~ Lᴬ → atoms '' s ~ (litters L)ᴬ

import Mathlib.Logic.Equiv.Defs
import ConNF.Base.NearLitter

/-!
# Base permutations

In this file, we define the group of *base permutations*, and their actions on atoms, litters, and
near-litters. In the paper, these are called *`-1`-allowable permutations*, but that term has a

of atoms pointwise to `s`, the resulting set of atoms is near the litter obtained by applying the

  atoms : Perm Atom

  atoms : Perm Atom

    π • L = πᴸ L :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem smul_nearLitter_atoms (π : BasePerm) (N : NearLitter) :
    (π • N)ᴬ = π • Nᴬ :=

@[simp]

/-- Nearness is symmetric. -/
@[symm]
theorem near_symm (h : s ~ t) : t ~ s := by
  rwa [Near, symmDiff_comm] at h

C1_dependencies.content:
/-- Nearness is transitive. -/
@[trans]
theorem near_trans (h₁ : s ~ t) (h₂ : t ~ u) : s ~ u :=
  (small_union h₁ h₂).mono (symmDiff_trans_subset s t u)

C1_dependencies.name: ConNF.litter_eq_of_near
C1_dependencies.content:
/-- If two litters are near each other, then they are equal. -/
theorem litter_eq_of_near {L₁ L₂ : Litter} (h : L₁ᴬ ~ L₂ᴬ) : L₁ = L₂ := by
  obtain ⟨a, ha₁, ha₂⟩ := inter_nonempty_of_near h L₁.atoms_not_small
  exact ha₁.symm.trans ha₂

theorem near_rfl : s ~ s :=

import Mathlib.Logic.Equiv.Defs
import ConNF.Base.NearLitter

/-!
# Base permutations

In this file, we define the group of *base permutations*, and their actions on atoms, litters, and
near-litters. In the paper, these are called *`-1`-allowable permutations*, but that term has a
different meaning in this formalisation.
-/

universe u

open Cardinal Equiv
open scoped Pointwise

namespace ConNF

variable [Params.{u}]

/-!
## Definitions
-/

/-- A *base permutation* consists of a permutation of atoms, a permutation of litters, and a proof
that if some set `s` is near the litter set of some litter `L`, then when we apply the permutation
of atoms pointwise to `s`, the resulting set of atoms is near the litter obtained by applying the
permutation of litters to `L`. This condition means that the pointwise image of a near-litter `N`
under the permutation of atoms is a near-litter, and that the litter it is near to is just the image
of `Nᴸ` under the permutation of litters. It is easy to see that it is not necessary to include
the litter permutation in this definition, because the image of some litter `L` under the
permutation of litters must be the unique litter near the pointwise image of `Lᴬ` under the map of
atoms; we simply include the data of this extra permutation for definitional convenience. -/
structure BasePerm where
  atoms : Perm Atom
  litters : Perm Litter
  apply_near_apply (s : Set Atom) (L : Litter) : s ~ Lᴬ → atoms '' s ~ (litters L)ᴬ

namespace BasePerm

/-- If `π` is a base permutation, we write `πᴬ` for its associated permutation of atoms. -/
instance : SuperA BasePerm (Perm Atom) where
  superA := atoms

/-- If `π` is a base permutation, we write `πᴸ` for its associated permutation of litters. -/
instance : SuperL BasePerm (Perm Litter) where
  superL := litters

/-- For a base permutation `π` and an atom `a`, we write `π • a` for `πᴬ a`.
We will later show that this is a group action. -/
instance : SMul BasePerm Atom where
  smul π a := πᴬ a

/-- For a base permutation `π` and a litter `L`, we write `π • L` for `πᴸ L`.
We will later show that this is a group action. -/
instance : SMul BasePerm Litter where
  smul π L := πᴸ L

/-- A restatement of `apply_near_apply` using the new notations. -/
theorem smul_near_smul (π : BasePerm) (s : Set Atom) (L : Litter) :
    s ~ Lᴬ → π • s ~ (π • L)ᴬ :=
  π.apply_near_apply s L

/-- For a base permutation `π` and an atom `N`, we write `π • N` for the near-litter `N'` such that
`N'ᴸ = π • Nᴸ` and `N'ᴬ = π • Nᴬ`, where the latter group action on sets of atoms is the pointwise
action. We will later show that this is a group action. -/
instance : SMul BasePerm NearLitter where
  smul π N := ⟨π • Nᴸ, π • Nᴬ, π.smul_near_smul Nᴬ Nᴸ N.atoms_near_litter⟩

/-! We establish some useful definitional equalities. -/

theorem smul_atom_def (π : BasePerm) (a : Atom) :
    π • a = πᴬ a :=
  rfl

theorem smul_litter_def (π : BasePerm) (L : Litter) :
    π • L = πᴸ L :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem smul_nearLitter_atoms (π : BasePerm) (N : NearLitter) :
    (π • N)ᴬ = π • Nᴬ :=
  rfl

theorem smul_nearLitter_litter (π : BasePerm) (N : NearLitter) :
    (π • N)ᴸ = π • Nᴸ := by exact?

C1_dependencies.name: rfl
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

import Mathlib.Logic.Equiv.Defs
import ConNF.Base.NearLitter

/-!
# Base permutations

In this file, we define the group of *base permutations*, and their actions on atoms, litters, and
near-litters. In the paper, these are called *`-1`-allowable permutations*, but that term has a
different meaning in this formalisation.
-/

universe u

open Cardinal Equiv
open scoped Pointwise

namespace ConNF

variable [Params.{u}]

/-!
## Definitions
-/

/-- A *base permutation* consists of a permutation of atoms, a permutation of litters, and a proof
that if some set `s` is near the litter set of some litter `L`, then when we apply the permutation
of atoms pointwise to `s`, the resulting set of atoms is near the litter obtained by applying the
permutation of litters to `L`. This condition means that the pointwise image of a near-litter `N`
under the permutation of atoms is a near-litter, and that the litter it is near to is just the image
of `Nᴸ` under the permutation of litters. It is easy to see that it is not necessary to include
the litter permutation in this definition, because the image of some litter `L` under the
permutation of litters must be the unique litter near the pointwise image of `Lᴬ` under the map of
atoms; we simply include the data of this extra permutation for definitional convenience. -/
structure BasePerm where
  atoms : Perm Atom
  litters : Perm Litter
  apply_near_apply (s : Set Atom) (L : Litter) : s ~ Lᴬ → atoms '' s ~ (litters L)ᴬ

namespace BasePerm

/-- If `π` is a base permutation, we write `πᴬ` for its associated permutation of atoms. -/
instance : SuperA BasePerm (Perm Atom) where
  superA := atoms

/-- If `π` is a base permutation, we write `πᴸ` for its associated permutation of litters. -/
instance : SuperL BasePerm (Perm Litter) where
  superL := litters

/-- For a base permutation `π` and an atom `a`, we write `π • a` for `πᴬ a`.
We will later show that this is a group action. -/
instance : SMul BasePerm Atom where
  smul π a := πᴬ a

/-- For a base permutation `π` and a litter `L`, we write `π • L` for `πᴸ L`.
We will later show that this is a group action. -/
instance : SMul BasePerm Litter where
  smul π L := πᴸ L

/-- A restatement of `apply_near_apply` using the new notations. -/
theorem smul_near_smul (π : BasePerm) (s : Set Atom) (L : Litter) :
    s ~ Lᴬ → π • s ~ (π • L)ᴬ :=
  π.apply_near_apply s L

/-- For a base permutation `π` and an atom `N`, we write `π • N` for the near-litter `N'` such that
`N'ᴸ = π • Nᴸ` and `N'ᴬ = π • Nᴬ`, where the latter group action on sets of atoms is the pointwise
action. We will later show that this is a group action. -/
instance : SMul BasePerm NearLitter where
  smul π N := ⟨π • Nᴸ, π • Nᴬ, π.smul_near_smul Nᴬ Nᴸ N.atoms_near_litter⟩

/-! We establish some useful definitional equalities. -/

theorem smul_atom_def (π : BasePerm) (a : Atom) :
    π • a = πᴬ a :=
  rfl

theorem smul_litter_def (π : BasePerm) (L : Litter) :
    π • L = πᴸ L :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem smul_nearLitter_atoms (π : BasePerm) (N : NearLitter) :
    (π • N)ᴬ = π • Nᴬ := by exact?

C1_dependencies.name: rfl
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

import Mathlib.Logic.Equiv.Defs
import ConNF.Base.NearLitter

/-!
# Base permutations

In this file, we define the group of *base permutations*, and their actions on atoms, litters, and
near-litters. In the paper, these are called *`-1`-allowable permutations*, but that term has a
different meaning in this formalisation.
-/

universe u

open Cardinal Equiv
open scoped Pointwise

namespace ConNF

variable [Params.{u}]

/-!
## Definitions
-/

/-- A *base permutation* consists of a permutation of atoms, a permutation of litters, and a proof
that if some set `s` is near the litter set of some litter `L`, then when we apply the permutation
of atoms pointwise to `s`, the resulting set of atoms is near the litter obtained by applying the
permutation of litters to `L`. This condition means that the pointwise image of a near-litter `N`
under the permutation of atoms is a near-litter, and that the litter it is near to is just the image
of `Nᴸ` under the permutation of litters. It is easy to see that it is not necessary to include
the litter permutation in this definition, because the image of some litter `L` under the
permutation of litters must be the unique litter near the pointwise image of `Lᴬ` under the map of
atoms; we simply include the data of this extra permutation for definitional convenience. -/
structure BasePerm where
  atoms : Perm Atom
  litters : Perm Litter
  apply_near_apply (s : Set Atom) (L : Litter) : s ~ Lᴬ → atoms '' s ~ (litters L)ᴬ

namespace BasePerm

/-- If `π` is a base permutation, we write `πᴬ` for its associated permutation of atoms. -/
instance : SuperA BasePerm (Perm Atom) where
  superA := atoms

/-- If `π` is a base permutation, we write `πᴸ` for its associated permutation of litters. -/
instance : SuperL BasePerm (Perm Litter) where
  superL := litters

/-- For a base permutation `π` and an atom `a`, we write `π • a` for `πᴬ a`.
We will later show that this is a group action. -/
instance : SMul BasePerm Atom where
  smul π a := πᴬ a

/-- For a base permutation `π` and a litter `L`, we write `π • L` for `πᴸ L`.
We will later show that this is a group action. -/
instance : SMul BasePerm Litter where
  smul π L := πᴸ L

/-- A restatement of `apply_near_apply` using the new notations. -/
theorem smul_near_smul (π : BasePerm) (s : Set Atom) (L : Litter) :
    s ~ Lᴬ → π • s ~ (π • L)ᴬ :=
  π.apply_near_apply s L

/-- For a base permutation `π` and an atom `N`, we write `π • N` for the near-litter `N'` such that
`N'ᴸ = π • Nᴸ` and `N'ᴬ = π • Nᴬ`, where the latter group action on sets of atoms is the pointwise
action. We will later show that this is a group action. -/
instance : SMul BasePerm NearLitter where
  smul π N := ⟨π • Nᴸ, π • Nᴬ, π.smul_near_smul Nᴬ Nᴸ N.atoms_near_litter⟩

/-! We establish some useful definitional equalities. -/

theorem smul_atom_def (π : BasePerm) (a : Atom) :
    π • a = πᴬ a :=
  rfl

    π • L = πᴸ L := by exact?

C1_dependencies.name: rfl
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

import Mathlib.Logic.Equiv.Defs
import ConNF.Base.NearLitter

/-!
# Base permutations

In this file, we define the group of *base permutations*, and their actions on atoms, litters, and
near-litters. In the paper, these are called *`-1`-allowable permutations*, but that term has a
different meaning in this formalisation.
-/

universe u

open Cardinal Equiv
open scoped Pointwise

namespace ConNF

variable [Params.{u}]

/-!
## Definitions
-/

/-- A *base permutation* consists of a permutation of atoms, a permutation of litters, and a proof
that if some set `s` is near the litter set of some litter `L`, then when we apply the permutation
of atoms pointwise to `s`, the resulting set of atoms is near the litter obtained by applying the
permutation of litters to `L`. This condition means that the pointwise image of a near-litter `N`
under the permutation of atoms is a near-litter, and that the litter it is near to is just the image
of `Nᴸ` under the permutation of litters. It is easy to see that it is not necessary to include
the litter permutation in this definition, because the image of some litter `L` under the
permutation of litters must be the unique litter near the pointwise image of `Lᴬ` under the map of
atoms; we simply include the data of this extra permutation for definitional convenience. -/
structure BasePerm where
  atoms : Perm Atom
  litters : Perm Litter
  apply_near_apply (s : Set Atom) (L : Litter) : s ~ Lᴬ → atoms '' s ~ (litters L)ᴬ

namespace BasePerm

/-- If `π` is a base permutation, we write `πᴬ` for its associated permutation of atoms. -/
instance : SuperA BasePerm (Perm Atom) where
  superA := atoms

/-- If `π` is a base permutation, we write `πᴸ` for its associated permutation of litters. -/
instance : SuperL BasePerm (Perm Litter) where
  superL := litters

/-- For a base permutation `π` and an atom `a`, we write `π • a` for `πᴬ a`.
We will later show that this is a group action. -/
instance : SMul BasePerm Atom where
  smul π a := πᴬ a

/-- For a base permutation `π` and a litter `L`, we write `π • L` for `πᴸ L`.
We will later show that this is a group action. -/
instance : SMul BasePerm Litter where
  smul π L := πᴸ L

/-- A restatement of `apply_near_apply` using the new notations. -/
theorem smul_near_smul (π : BasePerm) (s : Set Atom) (L : Litter) :
    s ~ Lᴬ → π • s ~ (π • L)ᴬ :=
  π.apply_near_apply s L

/-- For a base permutation `π` and an atom `N`, we write `π • N` for the near-litter `N'` such that
`N'ᴸ = π • Nᴸ` and `N'ᴬ = π • Nᴬ`, where the latter group action on sets of atoms is the pointwise
action. We will later show that this is a group action. -/
instance : SMul BasePerm NearLitter where
  smul π N := ⟨π • Nᴸ, π • Nᴬ, π.smul_near_smul Nᴬ Nᴸ N.atoms_near_litter⟩

/-! We establish some useful definitional equalities. -/

theorem smul_atom_def (π : BasePerm) (a : Atom) :
    π • a = πᴬ a := by exact?

C1_dependencies.name: rfl
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

/-!
# Base permutations

In this file, we define the group of *base permutations*, and their actions on atoms, litters, and
near-litters. In the paper, these are called *`-1`-allowable permutations*, but that term has a
different meaning in this formalisation.
-/

universe u

open Cardinal Equiv
open scoped Pointwise

namespace ConNF

variable [Params.{u}]

/-!
## Definitions
-/

/-- A *base permutation* consists of a permutation of atoms, a permutation of litters, and a proof
that if some set `s` is near the litter set of some litter `L`, then when we apply the permutation
of atoms pointwise to `s`, the resulting set of atoms is near the litter obtained by applying the
permutation of litters to `L`. This condition means that the pointwise image of a near-litter `N`
under the permutation of atoms is a near-litter, and that the litter it is near to is just the image
of `Nᴸ` under the permutation of litters. It is easy to see that it is not necessary to include
the litter permutation in this definition, because the image of some litter `L` under the
permutation of litters must be the unique litter near the pointwise image of `Lᴬ` under the map of
atoms; we simply include the data of this extra permutation for definitional convenience. -/
structure BasePerm where
  atoms : Perm Atom
  litters : Perm Litter

/-- If `π` is a base permutation, we write `πᴸ` for its associated permutation of litters. -/

  superL := litters

We will later show that this is a group action. -/
instance : SMul BasePerm Atom where
  smul π a := πᴬ a

We will later show that this is a group action. -/

# Base permutations

In this file, we define the group of *base permutations*, and their actions on atoms, litters, and
near-litters. In the paper, these are called *`-1`-allowable permutations*, but that term has a
different meaning in this formalisation.
-/

universe u

open Cardinal Equiv
open scoped Pointwise

namespace ConNF

variable [Params.{u}]

/-!
## Definitions
-/

that if some set `s` is near the litter set of some litter `L`, then when we apply the permutation
of atoms pointwise to `s`, the resulting set of atoms is near the litter obtained by applying the
permutation of litters to `L`. This condition means that the pointwise image of a near-litter `N`
under the permutation of atoms is a near-litter, and that the litter it is near to is just the image
of `Nᴸ` under the permutation of litters. It is easy to see that it is not necessary to include
the litter permutation in this definition, because the image of some litter `L` under the
permutation of litters must be the unique litter near the pointwise image of `Lᴬ` under the map of
atoms; we simply include the data of this extra permutation for definitional convenience. -/
structure BasePerm where
  atoms : Perm Atom
  litters : Perm Litter
  apply_near_apply (s : Set Atom) (L : Litter) : s ~ Lᴬ → atoms '' s ~ (litters L)ᴬ

instance : SuperA BasePerm (Perm Atom) where
  superA := atoms

instance : SuperL BasePerm (Perm Litter) where
  superL := litters

/-- For a base permutation `π` and an atom `a`, we write `π • a` for `πᴬ a`.
We will later show that this is a group action. -/
instance : SMul BasePerm Atom where
  smul π a := πᴬ a

We will later show that this is a group action. -/

  smul π L := πᴸ L

theorem smul_near_smul (π : BasePerm) (s : Set Atom) (L : Litter) :
    s ~ Lᴬ → π • s ~ (π • L)ᴬ := by exact?

/-!
# Base permutations

In this file, we define the group of *base permutations*, and their actions on atoms, litters, and
near-litters. In the paper, these are called *`-1`-allowable permutations*, but that term has a
different meaning in this formalisation.
-/

universe u

open Cardinal Equiv
open scoped Pointwise

namespace ConNF

variable [Params.{u}]

/-!
## Definitions

/-- A *base permutation* consists of a permutation of atoms, a permutation of litters, and a proof
that if some set `s` is near the litter set of some litter `L`, then when we apply the permutation
of atoms pointwise to `s`, the resulting set of atoms is near the litter obtained by applying the
permutation of litters to `L`. This condition means that the pointwise image of a near-litter `N`
under the permutation of atoms is a near-litter, and that the litter it is near to is just the image
of `Nᴸ` under the permutation of litters. It is easy to see that it is not necessary to include
the litter permutation in this definition, because the image of some litter `L` under the
permutation of litters must be the unique litter near the pointwise image of `Lᴬ` under the map of
atoms; we simply include the data of this extra permutation for definitional convenience. -/
structure BasePerm where
  atoms : Perm Atom
  litters : Perm Litter
  apply_near_apply (s : Set Atom) (L : Litter) : s ~ Lᴬ → atoms '' s ~ (litters L)ᴬ

import Mathlib.Logic.Equiv.Defs
import ConNF.Base.NearLitter

/-!
# Base permutations

In this file, we define the group of *base permutations*, and their actions on atoms, litters, and
near-litters. In the paper, these are called *`-1`-allowable permutations*, but that term has a
different meaning in this formalisation.
-/

universe u

open Cardinal Equiv
open scoped Pointwise

namespace ConNF

variable [Params.{u}]

/-!
## Definitions
-/

/-- A *base permutation* consists of a permutation of atoms, a permutation of litters, and a proof
that if some set `s` is near the litter set of some litter `L`, then when we apply the permutation
of atoms pointwise to `s`, the resulting set of atoms is near the litter obtained by applying the
permutation of litters to `L`. This condition means that the pointwise image of a near-litter `N`
under the permutation of atoms is a near-litter, and that the litter it is near to is just the image
of `Nᴸ` under the permutation of litters. It is easy to see that it is not necessary to include
the litter permutation in this definition, because the image of some litter `L` under the
permutation of litters must be the unique litter near the pointwise image of `Lᴬ` under the map of
atoms; we simply include the data of this extra permutation for definitional convenience. -/
structure BasePerm where
  atoms : Perm Atom
  litters : Perm Litter
  apply_near_apply (s : Set Atom) (L : Litter) : s ~ Lᴬ → atoms '' s ~ (litters L)ᴬ

/-- A set is a collection of elements of some type `α`.

Although `Set` is defined as `α → Prop`, this is an implementation detail which should not be
relied on. Instead, `setOf` and membership of a set (`∈`) should be used to convert between sets
and predicates.
-/
def Set (α : Type u) := α → Prop
